statement: In linear algebra, a rotation matrix is an n-dimensional transformation matrix R acting on Euclidean space ℝ^n that satisfies R^T = R^(-1) (orthogonality), with det R = 1 for a proper rotation and det R = -1 for an improper rotation (roto-reflection), used to rotate column vectors via premultiplication R x.

symbols.meaning: unit vector parallel to the rotation axis in ℝ^3
rotation angle about the rotation axis
vector being rotated in Euclidean space
cross product skew-symmetric matrix of axis u
outer product u u^T of axis u with itself

properties.why: A rotation matrix is an orthogonal matrix on ℝ^n

properties.property: det R = ±1 (det R = 1 for proper rotations, det R = -1 for improper rotations)
properties.why: Follows from orthogonality and distinguishes pure rotations from reflections

properties.property: R u = u in three dimensions, meaning u is an eigenvector with eigenvalue λ = 1
properties.why: A vector along the rotation axis is unchanged by the rotation

properties.property: tr(R) = 1 + 2 cos θ for a 3 × 3 rotation matrix
properties.why: The trace of R directly relates to the angle of rotation

properties.property: R = (cos θ) I + (sin θ) [u]_× + (1 - cos θ) (u ⊗ u)
properties.why: Matrix form of Rodrigues' rotation formula parametrizing a 3D rotation by axis u and angle θ

properties.property: Order of operations is right-to-left: R x = R_x(α) R_y(β) R_z(γ) x
properties.why: Matrix multiplication is non-commutative and rotation matrices premultiply column vectors

assumptions.assumption: Matrices premultiply column vectors in Euclidean space
assumptions.breaks_when: Row vectors or postmultiplication conventions are used, requiring matrix transposition and reversed multiplication order

assumptions.assumption: Axis vector u is a unit vector (u_x^2 + u_y^2 + u_z^2 = 1) for Rodrigues' formula
assumptions.breaks_when: The vector u is not normalized to unit length

failure_modes.mode: Degenerate axis extraction via skew-symmetric difference R - R^T
failure_modes.signature: R - R^T = 0, yielding a zero vector for u
failure_modes.cause: R is symmetric, corresponding to a rotation angle of 0° or 180° where sin θ = 0

failure_modes.mode: Angle sign ambiguity when using only matrix trace
failure_modes.signature: |θ| = arccos((tr(R) - 1) / 2) only provides the absolute value of the angle
failure_modes.cause: Cosine is an even function, requiring cross-product/skew-symmetric terms to determine orientation relative to the chosen axis
